subtitle: Do not call or press anything. This looks like a scam. The phone number is the warning sign, not something to call. It scares you with infection and a countdown, but the bottom line says it is only a demo page.
Every family has this phone call: "Where do I click?"
So I built Mate: a small light bulb on their Windows PC.
He shines a beam on the exact button. They click it themselves.

captions.text: "Where is the Pay now button?"  Typed for this take

subtitle: I cannot find a Pay now button on this screen. This is just your chats with Tom and family.
He never presses Pay. Never Delete. Nothing with a password.
And passwords are painted black before anything leaves the PC.
This is how I really work. Muse Voice Transcribe hears you. Muse Spark finds the button. MMS-TTS speaks. That is this voice. Every answer shows its model, its timing, and what was blacked out.
Seven Meta models. Each one has a job. You choose my brain: quick, careful, or open weights on our own GPU.
After each lesson, a card to keep. Muse Glimmer, Meta's open model on our own GPU, writes the steps. Muse Image draws the picture.
We measured it. On forty made-up pages, twenty of them scams, I caught all twenty.
When the button was on the screen and Windows listed it, I was right in all six hundred ten answers. Without that list, less than half. We report both numbers.
A son or daughter installs me once. A new app needs no new code where Windows lists its buttons. When a button isn't there, I say so.
One installer. No account to try. Try me at meta-mate dot stream. I light the button. You click it.
